body.en: An ideal *voltage* source keeps its terminal voltage constant for any load; its internal resistance is zero. A practical voltage source has a small series internal resistance r, so $V = E - Ir$. An ideal current source gives a constant current for any load; it has infinite internal resistance. A practical current source has a large resistance in parallel.
body.kn: ಆದರ್ಶ ವಿಭವ ಆಕರದ ಆಂತರಿಕ ರೋಧ ಶೂನ್ಯ; ಅದು ಸ್ಥಿರ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ನಿಜವಾದ ಆಕರದಲ್ಲಿ V = E − Ir. ಆದರ್ಶ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಆಕರದ ಆಂತರಿಕ ರೋಧ ಅನಂತ; ಅದು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Maximum power transfer

say.en: A real source is an ideal emf E in series with a small internal resistance r. Connect a load RL to its terminals.
The terminal voltage falls as current is drawn, because of the drop inside the source.
Plot the load power against RL for E = 12 volts and r = 4 ohms. It rises, peaks and falls. The peak is exactly at RL = r.
Then the maximum power is E squared over 4 r, here 9 watts. But half the power is lost inside, so efficiency is only 50 percent.
On the board: Maximum power transfer.

body.en: A voltage *source* E with series resistance r is equivalent, at its terminals, to a current source $I = E/r$ with the same r in parallel. Either form gives the same voltage and current in any load.

points.en: I = E/r, r moves from series to parallel

body.en: A source of internal (or Thevenin) resistance $R_s$ delivers *maximum power* to a load when $R_L = R_s$. Then $P_{max} = E^2/4R_s$ and the efficiency is only 50 %, because half the power is lost inside the source. This matching is used in amplifiers, speakers and antennas.

tagline.en: R, L and C on AC, inductive and capacitive reactance, phase relations, impedance of series RL, RC and RLC circuits, and true power and power factor.

myth.en: The element voltages in a series AC circuit must add up to the supply voltage, so V_R = 184 V, V_L = 368 V and V_C = 230 V on a 230 V supply cannot be right.

truth.en: The voltages are out of phase and must be added as phasors: $V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$. A single element can even have more voltage than the supply. In DC circuits plain addition always works, so it feels like a law. In AC, V_L and V_C point in opposite directions on the phasor diagram and partly cancel, while V_R is at right angles to both.

say.en: X_L = 2πfL rises with frequency; X_C = 1/(2πfC) falls with frequency.
Pure L: I lags V by 90°; pure C: I leads V by 90°; neither uses average power.
Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²); I = V/Z.
Power factor cos φ = R/Z; true power P = VI cos φ = I²R.
Series AC voltages add as phasors, not as numbers.

goal.en: R, L and C on AC, inductive and capacitive reactance, phase relations, impedance of series RL, RC and RLC circuits, and true power and power factor.

task.en: Does the current lead, lag or stay in phase with the voltage?

explain.en: Net inductive circuits have lagging current, net capacitive circuits leading current, and a purely resistive (or resonant) circuit has the current in phase.

takeaway.en: X_L = 2πfL rises with frequency; X_C = 1/(2πfC) falls with frequency.

headline.en: In RLC numericals, draw the impedance triangle (R across, X_L − X_C up, Z as the hypotenuse) and the voltage phasor diagram. State whether the power factor is lagging or leading; a bare number like '0.8' may lose half a mark.

narration.en: Many people think: The element voltages in a series AC circuit must add up to the supply voltage, so V_R = 184 V, V_L = 368 V and V_C = 230 V on a 230 V supply cannot be right. Actually: The voltages are out of phase and must be added as phasors: $V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$. A single element can even have more voltage than the supply. In DC circuits plain addition always works, so it feels like a law. In AC, V_L and V_C point in opposite directions on the phasor diagram and partly cancel, while V_R is at right angles to both.

problem.en: A 12 V battery with internal resistance 0.5 Ω supplies a 5.5 Ω load. Find the current and the terminal voltage.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 V battery with internal resistance 0.5 Ω supplies a 5.5 Ω load. Find the current and the terminal voltage.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 volts battery with internal resistance 0.5 ohms supplies a 5.5 ohms load. Find the current and the terminal voltage.
I equals E over R plus r equals 12 over 5.5 plus 0.5 equals 2 A.
V equals E - Ir equals 12 minus 2 times 0.5 equals 11 volts.
Check: V equals IR equals 2 times 5.5 equals 11 volts.
So the answer is 2 A; 11 volts.

problem.en: A 20 V source has internal resistance 4 Ω. Find the load for maximum power and the maximum power.

steps.en: For maximum power, R_L = R_s = 4 Ω.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 20 V source has internal resistance 4 Ω. Find the load for maximum power and the maximum power.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 20 volts source has internal resistance 4 ohms. Find the load for maximum power and the maximum power.
For maximum power, R L equals R s equals 4 ohms.
P max equals E squared/4R s equals 400 over 16 equals 25 watts.
Check: I equals 20 over 8 equals 2.5 A, P equals 2.5 squared times 4 equals 25 watts.
So the answer is R L equals 4 ohms; 25 watts.

points.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E = ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E/r.

points.en: Maximum power when R_L = R_s; P_max = E²/4R_s at 50 % efficiency.
points.kn: RL = Rs ಆದಾಗ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ; Pmax = E²/4Rs, ದಕ್ಷತೆ 50 %.

homework.en: Convert a 3 A current source with 5 Ω in parallel into a voltage source.

narration.en: Recap. An ideal voltage source has zero internal resistance; an ideal current source has infinite internal resistance. E in series with r equals E/r in parallel with r. Maximum power when R_L = R_s; P_max = E²/4R_s at 50 % efficiency.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಆದರ್ಶ ವಿಭವ ಆಕರಕ್ಕೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ, ಆದರ್ಶ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಆಕರಕ್ಕೆ ಅನಂತ ಆಂತರಿಕ ರೋಧ. ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E = ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E/r. RL = Rs ಆದಾಗ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ; Pmax = E²/4Rs, ದಕ್ಷತೆ 50 %.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. An ideal voltage source has zero internal resistance; an ideal current source has infinite internal resistance.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಆದರ್ಶ ವಿಭವ ಆಕರಕ್ಕೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ, ಆದರ್ಶ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಆಕರಕ್ಕೆ ಅನಂತ ಆಂತರಿಕ ರೋಧ.

say.en: E in series with r equals E over r in parallel with r.
say.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E equals ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ r ಇರುವ E over r.

say.en: Maximum power when R L equals R s; P max equals E squared/4R s at 50 percent efficiency.
say.kn: RL equals Rs ಆದಾಗ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ; Pmax equals E squared/4Rs, ದಕ್ಷತೆ 50 percent.

say.kn: ಮುಂದೆ: ಅಧ್ಯಾರೋಪಣ, ಥೆವೆನಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ನಾರ್ಟನ್ ಪ್ರಮೇಯಗಳು.
